_: Ask the running server what each tool does to your environment BEFORE calling it. The same four booleans ride on `tools/list` as MCP annotations (readOnlyHint / destructiveHint / idempotentHint / openWorldHint); this topic serves them in-band for clients that do not surface annotations, and for an agent deciding whether a failed call is safe to retry.

hint_semantics.read_only: the call does not modify its environment
hint_semantics.destructive: the call may overwrite or remove pre-existing state
hint_semantics.idempotent: repeating the call with the same arguments changes nothing further
hint_semantics.open_world: the call may interact with entities outside this machine

render_frameforge_yaml.title: Render FrameForge YAML
writes: resets this session's page-*.svg / p*.png and diagnostics.json

run_sdk_code.title: Run SDK code
writes: executes untrusted Python in an un-sandboxed subprocess
resets this session's page-*.svg / p*.png and diagnostics.json

expected.note: each tool declares whether it is read-only, destructive, idempotent, and open-world — the same values published as MCP tool annotations

how_to_read_it: read_only:true — free to call, and free to call again; this is what makes the discovery tools the cheap first step.
destructive:true — the call may destroy state you still want. Every render tool is destructive because it RESETS its session's previous pages: only the last call's artifacts remain.
idempotent:false — a retry is NOT free. run_sdk_code executes arbitrary Python; write_sdk_client with append=true adds more text each time.
open_world:true — only the two code-execution tools. Everything else renders locally and reaches nothing beyond this machine.

related.envelope: describe_capabilities(topic='envelope') — the shape every tool result satisfies, published as each tool's outputSchema and validated by the server before the result is sent
related.security: describe_capabilities(topic='security') — which filesystem roots the propose/measure tools may read
